brand_fidelity.evidence: The header is a Harbour #1F3A4D 'hull' with a 6px Signal #C2462B boot-stripe, and the keel-and-hull SVG mark and the centre 'keel line' on the balance bars tie the visuals to the name. Newsreader with Public Sans on a warm #F4F1EA paper ground reads steady and trustworthy, neither playful nor bank-like. The one tension is that 'owes' bars are filled in Signal red while 'is owed' gets calm navy, which nudges debt toward warning colour even though the copy says owing is normal.

visual_craft.evidence: Hierarchy is clear: serif h2s in Harbour, 48px controls, consistent 8–10px radii, tabular serif money figures, and a dark Settle up panel that reads as the conclusion. Several spots are uneven. 'Add person' wraps onto two lines at both widths. On desktop the sticky summary column starts about 400px down, leaving a big empty gap beside People. The preview slot leaves dead space above 'Add expense', and the expense amounts don't line up with the right edge of the Remove buttons.

copy_voice.evidence: Strings are plain and specific: 'Log who paid. See who owes whom.', 'Nobody's on this trip yet. Include yourself so your share counts too.', '2 payments and everyone's even.', 'Take Ana off the trip'. Errors say what to do, for example 'Use at most two decimal places, like 24.50.'. The duplicate-name error runs long ('Names can't match, even with different capitals, so try adding a last initial'), and 'Owing a little is…' hedges in a way that oddly implies owing a lot might not be normal.

ux_completeness.evidence: Every panel has a tailored empty state, and the Settle up note changes for no people, no expenses, all even, and N payments. It goes beyond the brief: a live split preview showing who gets the extra cent, Select everyone and Clear all controls, Undo after removing an expense, removing a person only when they aren't used in any expense, focus moving to the invalid field with input kept, and cross-tab sync. Transfers read as 'Chloe pays Ana $33.33' with a large amount, so they are easy to act on, and mobile stacks cleanly with no overflow.

code_quality.evidence: The money logic is solid: integer cents, sharesFor gives leftover cents in trip order via orderedSplit, a greedy largest-debtor-to-largest-creditor settle-up, robust parseAmount, and sanitize() on load. Accessibility is careful, with a fieldset and legend for the split, aria-invalid plus aria-describedby, role=alert slots, an sr-only status region, a skip link, and support for reduced motion. Small redundancies remain: --paper and --cream are the same value, there are overlapping margin rules for #people-empty, and ARROW_SVG is injected with innerHTML.

directed_design.evidence: The nautical idea is carried through with restraint: boot-stripe header, keel mark, a centre keel line splitting 'owes' and 'is owed', and a Harbour Settle up panel. The type pairing and warm paper ground are clear choices rather than defaults. The initial-avatar pills, dashed empty-state boxes and the awkward right-column gap feel less directed.

ai_tells: Pill chips (border-radius:999px) with initial-letter avatars for people, a common template pattern
Banner-style section comments in JS ('/* ---------- state & storage ---------- */')
Redundant CSS custom properties: --paper and --cream are both #F4F1EA
brand_violations: Signal red fills the 'owes' balance bars and the debtor-to-creditor transfer icons while 'is owed' gets calm navy, which frames owing in warning colour against the principle that owing money is normal
review.best_detail: The balance bars split around a centre 'keel line', with an '← owes | is owed →' axis, turning the brand name into a working, readable visualisation of who is up and who is down.
review.worst_detail: On desktop the sticky summary column renders far down the page, leaving a large empty gap beside the People panel, and the 'Add person' button wraps awkwardly onto two lines.
